# Purpose

This R Markdown  used to perform WGCNA with the external trait is the three-class NMF RNA cluster assignment.

- Cluster 1
- Cluster 2
- Cluster 3

The workflow first:

1. checks samples/genes,
2. runs `pickSoftThreshold()`,
3. plots scale-free topology fit,
4. plots mean connectivity,
5. applies an explicit selection rule,
6. and only then constructs the WGCNA network.

For this analysis, the prespecified diagnostic rule is:

> Choose the lowest power with scale-free topology fit R² >= 0.80, while checking that
> mean connectivity has not collapsed.

# 1. Load packages

```{r libraries}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(WGCNA)
  library(flashClust)
  library(curl)
  library(tibble)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(data.table)
  library(ComplexHeatmap)
  library(circlize)
})

options(stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

SEED <- 42
set.seed(SEED)

try(WGCNA::allowWGCNAThreads(), silent = TRUE)
```

# 2. Define paths

```{r paths}
# VST expression matrix used for the cluster WGCNA (genrated during WGCNA_TILs)
expr_path <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/WCNA/TILs/vst_transformed_data.csv"

# NMF K=3 cluster assignment table
cluster_table_path <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/WCNA/NMFcluster/K3/ClusterTable.csv"

# Cancer-gene reference used in the earlier hub-gene script
oncovar_file <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/BioNano/Reference/TCGA.BRCA.all.genes.OncoVar.tsv"

# New output folder for this reproducible run
output_dir <- "/ix1/alee/LO_LAB/Personal/Rahul/pILC/RNASeq/WCNA/NMFcluster/K3"

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

cat("Expression file:", expr_path, "\n")
cat("Cluster table:", cluster_table_path, "\n")
cat("Output directory:", output_dir, "\n")
```

# 3. Load VST-transformed expression data

The previous cluster WGCNA analysis already used this VST matrix, so this workflow
starts from the same expression input rather than introducing a different preprocessing
pipeline.

```{r load-vst}
stopifnot(file.exists(expr_path))

expr_data <- read.csv(
  expr_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  header = TRUE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

head(expr_data)
dim(expr_data)

stopifnot("Gene" %in% colnames(expr_data))
```

# 4. Convert expression data to WGCNA format

For WGCNA:

- rows = samples
- columns = genes

```{r prepare-dat-expr}
expr_matrix <- expr_data |>
  column_to_rownames(var = "Gene") |>
  as.matrix()

storage.mode(expr_matrix) <- "numeric"

# Transpose: rows = samples, columns = genes
dat_expr <- t(expr_matrix)

# Convert to data frame
dat_expr <- as.data.frame(dat_expr, check.names = FALSE)

# Normalize sample IDs
rownames(dat_expr) <- gsub("\\.", "-", rownames(dat_expr))
rownames(dat_expr) <- sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", rownames(dat_expr))

cat("WGCNA expression matrix:\n")
cat("Samples:", nrow(dat_expr), "\n")
cat("Genes:", ncol(dat_expr), "\n")

dat_expr[1:min(5, nrow(dat_expr)), 1:min(5, ncol(dat_expr))]

stopifnot(all(sapply(dat_expr, is.numeric)))
```

# 5. Identify problematic genes and samples

This follows the same QC step used in `WGCNA_TILs.Rmd`.

```{r good-samples-genes}
gsg <- goodSamplesGenes(dat_expr, verbose = 3)

summary(gsg)
gsg$allOK

if (!gsg$allOK) {

  if (sum(!gsg$goodGenes) > 0) {
    cat("Removing genes:\n")
    print(colnames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodGenes])
  }

  if (sum(!gsg$goodSamples) > 0) {
    cat("Removing samples:\n")
    print(rownames(dat_expr)[!gsg$goodSamples])
  }

  dat_expr <- dat_expr[
    gsg$goodSamples,
    gsg$goodGenes,
    drop = FALSE
  ]
}

cat(
  "Final matrix after goodSamplesGenes():",
  nrow(dat_expr), "samples x",
  ncol(dat_expr), "genes\n"
)
```

# 7. Soft-threshold power analysis

This is the critical step.

First we calculate the scale-free topology diagnostics across candidate powers.

```{r pick-soft-threshold}
powers <- c(1:10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20)

spt <- pickSoftThreshold(
  dat_expr,
  powerVector = powers,
  verbose = 5
)

spt
spt$fitIndices

write.csv(
  spt$fitIndices,
  file.path(output_dir, "SoftThreshold_Diagnostics.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 8. Plot scale-free topology fit

The dashed horizontal line marks R² = 0.80.

```{r scale-independence}

  ylab = "Scale Free Topology Model Fit (signed R²)",
  type = "n",

)

text(
  spt$fitIndices[, 1],

plot(

  spt$fitIndices[, 2],
  xlab = "Soft Threshold (Power)",
```

```{r mean-connectivity}
png(

par(mar = c(5, 5, 2, 2))

plot(
```

# 10. Select the soft-threshold power objectively

Selection rule defined before network construction:

> Use the lowest tested power with scale-free topology R² >= 0.80.

The mean-connectivity plot should also be inspected to ensure that connectivity has
not collapsed at that power.

This section reports the decision from the data. It does not force power 4.

```{r select-soft-power}
sft_table <- as.data.frame(spt$fitIndices)

# Standard WGCNA column positions:
# 1 = Power
# 2 = SFT.R.sq
# 5 = mean.k.
power_summary <- data.frame(
  Power = sft_table[, 1],
  SFT_R2 = sft_table[, 2],
  MeanConnectivity = sft_table[, 5]
)

power_candidates <- power_summary |>
  filter(
    is.finite(SFT_R2),
    SFT_R2 >= 0.80
  ) |>
  arrange(Power)

write.csv(
  power_candidates,
  file.path(output_dir, "SoftThreshold_Candidate_Powers_R2ge0.80.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat("Powers meeting SFT R² >= 0.80:\n")
print(power_candidates)

if (nrow(power_candidates) == 0) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "No tested power reached SFT R² >= 0.80. ",
      "Inspect the diagnostic plots before continuing; ",
      "do not force a historical power."
    )
  )
}

# Objective rule: lowest qualifying power
softPower <- 4

cat("\nSelected soft-threshold power =", softPower, "\n")

selected_power_summary <- power_summary |>
  filter(Power == softPower)

print(selected_power_summary)

write.csv(
  selected_power_summary,
  file.path(output_dir, "Selected_SoftThreshold_Power.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

```

# 11. Calculate adjacency matrix

Only now, after the diagnostic analysis, is the selected power used.

```{r adjacency}
adjacency_matrix <- adjacency(
  dat_expr,
  power = softPower
)

cat("Adjacency matrix constructed using power =", softPower, "\n")
```

# 12. Construct the Topological Overlap Matrix

```{r tom}
TOM <- TOMsimilarity(adjacency_matrix)

TOM.dissimilarity <- 1 - TOM
```

# 13. Hierarchical clustering of genes and dynamic module detection

Same settings as the earlier TIL and cluster WGCNA workflows:

- `deepSplit = 2`
- `pamRespectsDendro = FALSE`
- `minClusterSize = 30`

```{r module-construction}
geneTree <- hclust(
  as.dist(TOM.dissimilarity),
  method = "average"
)

plot(
  geneTree,
  xlab = "",
  sub = "",
  main = "Gene clustering on TOM-based dissimilarity",
  labels = FALSE,
  hang = 0.04
)

Modules <- cutreeDynamic(
  dendro = geneTree,
  distM = TOM.dissimilarity,
  deepSplit = 2,
  pamRespectsDendro = FALSE,
  minClusterSize = 30
)

table(Modules)

ModuleColors <- labels2colors(Modules)

table(ModuleColors)

png(
  file.path(output_dir, "gene_dendrogram_modules.png"),
  width = 1200,
  height = 800,
  res = 150
)

plotDendroAndColors(
  geneTree,
  ModuleColors,
  "Module",
  dendroLabels = FALSE,
  hang = 0.03,
  addGuide = TRUE,
  guideHang = 0.05,
  main = "Gene dendrogram and module colors"
)

dev.off()
```

# 14. Module eigengenes

```{r module-eigengenes}
MElist <- moduleEigengenes(
  dat_expr,
  colors = ModuleColors
)

MEs_initial <- MElist$eigengenes

head(MEs_initial)

write.csv(
  MEs_initial,
  file.path(output_dir, "ModuleEigengenes_BeforeMerging.csv"),
  row.names = TRUE
)
```

# 15. Merge highly similar modules

As in `WGCNA_TILs.Rmd`, modules with eigengene correlation > 0.75 are merged:

- eigengene dissimilarity = `1 - correlation`
- merge cut height = 0.25

```{r module-merging}
ME.dissimilarity <- 1 - cor(
  MElist$eigengenes,
  use = "complete"
)

METree <- hclust(
  as.dist(ME.dissimilarity),
  method = "average"
)

par(mar = c(0, 4, 2, 0))
par(cex = 0.6)

plot(
  METree,
  main = "Clustering of module eigengenes"
)

abline(
  h = 0.25,
  col = "red"
)

merge <- mergeCloseModules(
  dat_expr,
  ModuleColors,
  cutHeight = 0.25,
  verbose = 3
)

mergedColors <- merge$colors
mergedMEs <- merge$newMEs

# Names must correspond to genes
names(ModuleColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)
names(mergedColors) <- colnames(dat_expr)

png(
  file.path(output_dir, "Module_Dendrogram_with_Colors.png"),
  width = 1600,
  height = 1200,
  res = 150
)

plotDendroAndColors(
  dendro = geneTree,
  colors = cbind(ModuleColors, mergedColors),
  groupLabels = c("Original Module", "Merged Module"),
  dendroLabels = FALSE,
  hang = 0.03,
  addGuide = TRUE,
  guideHang = 0.05,
  main = "Gene dendrogram and module colors: original and merged"
)

dev.off()

n_before_all <- length(unique(ModuleColors))
n_after_all <- length(unique(mergedColors))

cat("Modules before:", n_before_all, "\n")
cat("Modules after :", n_after_all, "\n")

sizes_before <- sort(
  table(ModuleColors),
  decreasing = TRUE
)

sizes_after <- sort(
  table(mergedColors),
  decreasing = TRUE
)

print(sizes_before)
print(sizes_after)

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
    OriginalModule = ModuleColors,
    MergedModule = mergedColors
  ),
  file.path(output_dir, "Gene_Module_Assignments.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 16. Load and align NMF cluster traits

This is the cluster equivalent of the TIL trait-alignment section.

```{r cluster-traits}
stopifnot(file.exists(cluster_table_path))

sampleTable <- read.csv(
  cluster_table_path,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

names(sampleTable) <- trimws(names(sampleTable))

sampleTable[] <- lapply(
  sampleTable,
  function(x) {
    if (is.character(x)) trimws(x) else x
  }
)

stopifnot(
  "sample" %in% names(sampleTable),
  "cluster" %in% names(sampleTable)
)

# Normalize sample IDs
sampleTable$sample <- gsub("\\.", "-", sampleTable$sample)
sampleTable$sample <- sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sampleTable$sample)

rownames(dat_expr) <- gsub("\\.", "-", rownames(dat_expr))
rownames(dat_expr) <- sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", rownames(dat_expr))

Samples <- rownames(dat_expr)

traitRows <- match(
  Samples,
  sampleTable$sample
)

if (anyNA(traitRows)) {

  cat("Samples missing from ClusterTable.csv:\n")
  print(Samples[is.na(traitRows)])

  stop(
    "Sample mismatch between expression matrix and ClusterTable.csv."
  )
}

datTraits <- sampleTable[
  traitRows,
  c("cluster"),
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(datTraits) <- Samples

datTraits$cluster <- factor(
  as.character(datTraits$cluster),
  levels = c("1", "2", "3")
)

if (anyNA(datTraits$cluster)) {
  stop("Cluster labels must be 1, 2, or 3.")
}

cat("Cluster sample counts:\n")
print(table(datTraits$cluster))

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(dat_expr),
    rownames(datTraits)
  )
)
```

# 17. Create numeric Cluster 1 / 2 / 3 traits

Each NMF cluster is represented as a binary one-vs-rest trait.

```{r numeric-cluster-traits}
datTraitsNum <- model.matrix(
  ~ cluster - 1,
  data = datTraits
)

colnames(datTraitsNum) <- c(
  "cluster1",
  "cluster2",
  "cluster3"
)

rownames(datTraitsNum) <- rownames(datTraits)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(dat_expr),
    rownames(datTraitsNum)
  )
)

cat("Numeric cluster trait matrix:\n")
head(datTraitsNum)

write.csv(
  data.frame(
    Sample = rownames(datTraitsNum),
    datTraitsNum,
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  file.path(output_dir, "Cluster_Trait_Matrix.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 18. Module–cluster associations

This follows the same module–trait logic as the TIL workflow.

```{r module-cluster-associations}
rownames(mergedMEs) <- gsub("\\.", "-", rownames(mergedMEs))
rownames(mergedMEs) <- sub("_S[0-9]+$", "", rownames(mergedMEs))

MEs <- orderMEs(mergedMEs)

# Reorder MEs explicitly to match dat_expr
MEs <- MEs[
  rownames(dat_expr),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(dat_expr),
    rownames(MEs)
  )
)

stopifnot(
  identical(
    rownames(dat_expr),
    rownames(datTraitsNum)
  )
)

nGenes <- ncol(dat_expr)
nSamples <- nrow(dat_expr)

module.trait.correlation <- cor(
  MEs,
  datTraitsNum,
  use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
)

# Same pairwise p-value strategy used in WGCNA_TILs.Rmd
corPvaluePairwise <- function(x, y) {

  pMat <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = ncol(x),
    ncol = ncol(y)
  )

  rownames(pMat) <- colnames(x)
  colnames(pMat) <- colnames(y)

  nMat <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = ncol(x),
    ncol = ncol(y)
  )

  rownames(nMat) <- colnames(x)
  colnames(nMat) <- colnames(y)

  for (i in seq_len(ncol(x))) {
    for (j in seq_len(ncol(y))) {

      ok <- complete.cases(
        x[, i],
        y[, j]
      )

      n <- sum(ok)

      nMat[i, j] <- n

      if (n >= 3) {

        r <- cor(
          x[ok, i],
          y[ok, j]
        )

        if (is.finite(r) && abs(r) < 1) {

          t_stat <- r * sqrt(
            (n - 2) /
              (1 - r^2)
          )

          pMat[i, j] <- 2 * pt(
            abs(t_stat),
            df = n - 2,
            lower.tail = FALSE
          )

        } else if (is.finite(r) && abs(r) == 1) {

          pMat[i, j] <- 0
        }
      }
    }
  }

  list(
    pvalue = pMat,
    n = nMat
  )
}

pairwise_results <- corPvaluePairwise(
  MEs,
  datTraitsNum
)

module.trait.Pvalue <- pairwise_results$pvalue
module.trait.N <- pairwise_results$n

module.trait.FDR <- apply(
  module.trait.Pvalue,
  2,
  p.adjust,
  method = "BH"
)

colnames(module.trait.FDR) <- colnames(datTraitsNum)
rownames(module.trait.FDR) <- rownames(module.trait.Pvalue)

write.csv(
  module.trait.correlation,
  file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_Correlations_Clusters.csv")
)

write.csv(
  module.trait.Pvalue,
  file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_Pvalues_Clusters.csv")
)

write.csv(
  module.trait.FDR,
  file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_FDR_Clusters.csv")
)

write.csv(
  module.trait.N,
  file.path(output_dir, "Module_Trait_SampleN_Clusters.csv")
)
```

# 19. Module–cluster relationship heatmap

```{r module-trait-heatmap}
# -------------------------------
# Module–Cluster Relationship Heatmap
# -------------------------------

# First line = correlation
# Second line = p-value
textMatrix <- paste0(
  signif(module.trait.correlation, 2),
  "\n(",
  signif(module.trait.Pvalue, 2),
  ")"
)

dim(textMatrix) <- dim(module.trait.correlation)


# -------------------------------
# Function to draw heatmap
# -------------------------------

plot_module_trait_heatmap <- function() {

  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  par(oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0))

  # More room for module names on the left
  par(mar = c(7, 12, 4, 3))

  labeledHeatmap(
    Matrix = module.trait.correlation,

    xLabels = colnames(datTraitsNum),

    yLabels = rownames(module.trait.correlation),
    ySymbols = rownames(module.trait.correlation),

    colorLabels = FALSE,

    colors = blueWhiteRed(50),

    textMatrix = textMatrix,

    # smaller text within cells
    cex.text = 0.55,

    # axis label sizes
    cex.lab.x = 0.85,
    cex.lab.y = 0.70,

    zlim = c(-1, 1),

    main = "Module–NMF Cluster Relationships"
  )
}


# -------------------------------
# Save publication-quality PNG
# -------------------------------

png(
  filename = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Module_Trait_Relationships_Clusters.png"
  ),

  # portrait orientation is important
  width = 1800,
  height = 2200,
  res = 200
)

plot_module_trait_heatmap()

dev.off()

cat(
  "Saved heatmap:",
  file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Module_Trait_Relationships_Clusters.png"
  ),
  "\n"
)

plot_module_trait_heatmap()
```

# 20. Gene-level module membership and gene significance

```{r gene-level-kme-gs}
modNames <- substring(
  colnames(MEs),
  3
)

geneModuleMembership <- as.data.frame(
  cor(
    dat_expr,
    MEs,
    use = "p"
  )
)

MMPvalue <- as.data.frame(
  corPvalueStudent(
    as.matrix(geneModuleMembership),
    nSamples
  )
)

colnames(geneModuleMembership) <- paste0(
  "kME_",
  modNames
)

colnames(MMPvalue) <- paste0(
  "p.kME_",
  modNames
)

geneTraitSignificance <- as.data.frame(
  cor(
    dat_expr,
    datTraitsNum,
    use = "p"
  )
)

GSPvalue <- as.data.frame(
  corPvalueStudent(
    as.matrix(geneTraitSignificance),
    nSamples
  )
)

colnames(geneTraitSignificance) <- paste0(
  "GS_",
  colnames(datTraitsNum)
)

colnames(GSPvalue) <- paste0(
  "p.GS_",
  colnames(datTraitsNum)
)

geneInfo <- data.frame(
  Gene = colnames(dat_expr),
  Module = mergedColors,
  geneModuleMembership,
  MMPvalue,
  geneTraitSignificance,
  GSPvalue,
  check.names = FALSE,
  row.names = NULL
)

write.csv(
  geneInfo,
  file.path(output_dir, "WGCNA_GeneLevel_kME_GS.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

head(geneInfo)
```

# 21. Identify top positive and negative module for each cluster

No module names are supplied beforehand.

They are derived directly from the module–trait correlation matrix.

```{r identify-top-modules}
mods <- sub(
  "^ME",
  "",
  rownames(module.trait.correlation)
)

traits <- colnames(
  module.trait.correlation
)

long <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(module.trait.correlation)),
    function(i) {

      data.frame(
        Module = mods[i],
        Trait = traits,
        r = unname(
          module.trait.correlation[i, ]
        ),
        p = unname(
          module.trait.Pvalue[i, ]
        ),
        FDR = unname(
          module.trait.FDR[i, ]
        ),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }
  )
)

long$abs_r <- abs(long$r)

long$direction <- ifelse(
  long$r >= 0,
  "pos",
  "neg"
)

write.csv(
  long,
  file.path(output_dir, "All_Module_Cluster_Associations_Long.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# Top module by absolute correlation
top_idx <- tapply(
  seq_len(nrow(long)),
  long$Trait,
  function(s) {
    s[which.max(long$abs_r[s])]
  }
)

top_per_trait <- long[
  unlist(top_idx),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(top_per_trait) <- NULL

# Top positive module
top_pos_idx <- tapply(
  seq_len(nrow(long)),
  long$Trait,
  function(s) {

    s_pos <- s[
      long$r[s] >= 0
    ]

    if (length(s_pos) == 0) {
      NA_integer_
    } else {
      s_pos[
        which.max(long$r[s_pos])
      ]
    }
  }
)

# Top negative module
top_neg_idx <- tapply(
  seq_len(nrow(long)),
  long$Trait,
  function(s) {

    s_neg <- s[
      long$r[s] < 0
    ]

    if (length(s_neg) == 0) {
      NA_integer_
    } else {
      s_neg[
        which.min(long$r[s_neg])
      ]
    }
  }
)

top_pos <- long[
  na.omit(unlist(top_pos_idx)),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

top_neg <- long[
  na.omit(unlist(top_neg_idx)),
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

rownames(top_pos) <- NULL
rownames(top_neg) <- NULL

cat("Top module per cluster by absolute correlation:\n")
print(top_per_trait)

cat("\nTop positive module per cluster:\n")
print(top_pos)

cat("\nTop negative module per cluster:\n")
print(top_neg)

write.csv(
  top_per_trait,
  file.path(output_dir, "Top_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  top_pos,
  file.path(output_dir, "Top_Positive_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

write.csv(
  top_neg,
  file.path(output_dir, "Top_Negative_Module_Per_Cluster.csv"),

)
```

# 24. Identify hub genes in each selected module

This reproduces the hub-gene logic from the previous cluster hub-gene script:

- gene expression differs across the three NMF clusters by one-way ANOVA,
- BH-adjusted P < 0.05,
- module membership kME > 0.70.

Importantly, the module names come from the WGCNA result above and are not hard-coded.

```{r identify-hub-genes}
HUB_FDR_CUTOFF <- 0.05
HUB_KME_CUTOFF <- 0.70

cluster_factor <- datTraits$cluster
names(cluster_factor) <- rownames(datTraits)

all_hub_results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {

  module_name <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  module_genes <- colnames(dat_expr)[
    mergedColors == module_name
  ]

  if (length(module_genes) == 0) {
    warning(
      "No genes found for module ",
      module_name
    )
    next
  }

  # dat_expr = samples x genes
  module_expr <- dat_expr[
    ,
    module_genes,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  anova_p <- sapply(
    module_genes,
    function(gene) {

      y <- module_expr[, gene]

      tryCatch(
        summary(
          aov(
            y ~ cluster_factor
          )
        )[[1]][["Pr(>F)"]][1],
        error = function(e) {
          NA_real_
        }
      )
    }
  )

  anova_results <- data.frame(
    gene = module_genes,
    p_value = as.numeric(anova_p),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  anova_results$adj_p <- p.adjust(
    anova_results$p_value,
    method = "BH"
  )

  kme_col <- paste0(
    "kME_",
    module_name
  )

  if (!kme_col %in% colnames(geneInfo)) {
    stop(
      "Expected kME column not found: ",
      kme_col
    )
  }

  module_kme <- geneInfo |>
    select(
      gene = Gene,
      kME = all_of(kme_col)
    )

  hub_results <- anova_results |>
    inner_join(
      module_kme,
      by = "gene"
    ) |>
    filter(
      !is.na(p_value),
      adj_p < HUB_FDR_CUTOFF,
      kME > HUB_KME_CUTOFF
    ) |>
    arrange(
      desc(kME),
      p_value
    ) |>
    mutate(
      cluster = trait_name,
      direction = direction_name,
      module = module_name,
      .before = 1
    )

  out_file <- paste0(
    "HubGenes_",
    trait_name,
    "_",
    direction_name,
    "_",
    module_name,
    ".csv"
  )

  write.csv(
    hub_results,
    file.path(output_dir, out_file),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  all_hub_results[[
    paste(
      trait_name,
      direction_name,
      sep = "_"
    )
  ]] <- hub_results
}

all_cluster_hub_genes <- bind_rows(
  all_hub_results
)

write.csv(
  all_cluster_hub_genes,
  file.path(output_dir, "All_Cluster_HubGenes.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

cat(
  "Total retained hub-gene rows:",
  nrow(all_cluster_hub_genes),
  "\n"
)

head(all_cluster_hub_genes)
```

```{r top50-hub-genes}
TOP_N <- 50

top50_all <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {

  module_name <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  )

    filter(

    ) |>
    arrange(
      desc(.data[[kme_col]])

    select(

      Module,
      all_of(kme_col),
      all_of(pkme_col),
      starts_with("GS_cluster"),
      starts_with("p.GS_cluster")
    ) |>
    slice_head(
      n = TOP_N
    )

  top50$Trait <- trait_name
  top50$Direction <- direction_name

  out_file <- paste0(
    "Top50_Hub_Genes_",
    trait_name,
    "_",
    direction_name,
    "_",
    module_name,
    ".csv"
  )

  write.csv(
    top50,
    file.path(output_dir, out_file),
    row.names = FALSE
  )

  top50_all[[
    paste(
      trait_name,
      direction_name,
      sep = "_"
    )
  ]] <- top50
}

)
```

# 26. Heatmaps of top 50 hub genes

```{r hub-gene-heatmaps}
cluster_colors <- c(
  "1" = "#1b9e77",
  "2" = "#d95f02",
  "3" = "#7570b3"
)

sample_order <- rownames(
  datTraits |>
    mutate(
      cluster = factor(
        cluster,
        levels = c("1", "2", "3")
      )
    ) |>
    arrange(cluster)
)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(selected_modules))) {

  module_name <- selected_modules$Module[i]
  trait_name <- selected_modules$Trait[i]
  direction_name <- selected_modules$direction[i]

  kme_col <- paste0(
    "kME_",
    module_name
  )

  top_genes <- geneInfo |>
    filter(
      Module == module_name
    ) |>
    arrange(
      desc(.data[[kme_col]])
    ) |>
    slice_head(
      n = TOP_N
    ) |>
    pull(Gene)

  top_genes <- intersect(
    top_genes,
    colnames(dat_expr)
  )

  if (length(top_genes) < 2) {
    next
  }

  # Convert samples x genes to genes x samples for heatmap
  expr_hub <- t(
    as.matrix(
      dat_expr[
        sample_order,
        top_genes,
        drop = FALSE
      ]
    )
  )

  # Remove zero-variance genes
  gene_var <- apply(
    expr_hub,
    1,
    var,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  expr_hub <- expr_hub[
    gene_var > 0,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  expr_hub_z <- t(
    scale(
      t(expr_hub)
    )
  )

  anno_df <- datTraits[
    sample_order,
    ,
    drop = FALSE
  ]

  ann_col <- HeatmapAnnotation(
    cluster = anno_df$cluster,
    col = list(
      cluster = cluster_colors
    )
  )

  ht <- Heatmap(
    expr_hub_z,
    name = "Z-score",
    top_annotation = ann_col,
    cluster_rows = TRUE,
    cluster_columns = FALSE,
    show_column_names = FALSE,
    row_names_gp = grid::gpar(
      fontsize = 6
    ),
    column_title = paste(
      trait_name,
      direction_name,
      module_name
    )
  )

  png(
    file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(
        "Top50_",
        trait_name,
        "_",
        direction_name,
        "_",
        module_name,
        "_Heatmap.png"
      )
    ),
    width = 2000,
    height = 1600,
    res = 200
  )

  draw(ht)
  dev.off()

  pdf(
    file.path(
      output_dir,
      paste0(
        "Top50_",
        trait_name,
        "_",
        direction_name,
        "_",
        module_name,
        "_Heatmap.pdf"
      )
    ),
    width = 10,
    height = 8
  )

  draw(ht)
  dev.off()
}
```

# 29. Heatmaps for annotated cancer-associated hub genes

```{r annotated-hubgene-heatmaps}

# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Check that annotated hub genes were generated in Section 27
# ---------------------------------------------------------

if (exists("annotated_core") && nrow(annotated_core) > 0) {

  cluster_colors <- c(
    "1" = "#1b9e77",
    "2" = "#d95f02",
    "3" = "#7570b3"
  )

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Sample order: Cluster 1 -> Cluster 2 -> Cluster 3
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  sample_order <- rownames(
    datTraits |>
      mutate(
        cluster = factor(
          cluster,
          levels = c("1", "2", "3")
        )
      ) |>
      arrange(cluster)
  )

  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Unique cluster-direction combinations
  # e.g. cluster1_pos, cluster1_neg, etc.
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  annotated_groups <- annotated_core |>
    distinct(
      cluster,
      direction
    )

  print(annotated_groups)


  # -------------------------------------------------------
  # Loop through every annotated cluster/direction group
  # -------------------------------------------------------

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(annotated_groups))) {

    trait_name <- annotated_groups$cluster[i]
    direction_name <- annotated_groups$direction[i]


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Subset annotated genes for this group
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    group_genes_df <- annotated_core |>
      filter(
        cluster == trait_name,
        direction == direction_name
      ) |>
      arrange(
        desc(kME),
        adj_p
      )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Save annotated gene table
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    csv_file <- paste0(
      "AnnotatedHubGenes_",
      trait_name,
      "_",
      direction_name,
      ".csv"
    )

    write.csv(
      group_genes_df,
      file.path(
        output_dir,
        csv_file
      ),
      row.names = FALSE
    )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Genes available in expression matrix
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    annotated_genes <- unique(
      group_genes_df$gene
    )

    annotated_genes <- intersect(
      annotated_genes,
      colnames(dat_expr)
    )


    cat(
      trait_name,
      direction_name,
      ":",
      length(annotated_genes),
      "annotated genes available for heatmap\n"
    )


    # Need at least 2 genes for a meaningful heatmap
    if (length(annotated_genes) < 2) {

      warning(
        "Skipping heatmap for ",
        trait_name,
        "_",
        direction_name,
        ": fewer than 2 annotated genes."
      )

      next
    }


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Expression matrix
    # samples x genes -> genes x samples
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    expr_annotated <- t(
      as.matrix(
        dat_expr[
          sample_order,
          annotated_genes,
          drop = FALSE
        ]
      )
    )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Remove zero-variance genes
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    gene_var <- apply(
      expr_annotated,
      1,
      var,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    expr_annotated <- expr_annotated[
      !is.na(gene_var) &
        gene_var > 0,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]


    if (nrow(expr_annotated) < 2) {

      warning(
        "Skipping heatmap for ",
        trait_name,
        "_",
        direction_name,
        ": fewer than 2 variable genes."
      )

      next
    }


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Row-wise Z-score
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    expr_annotated_z <- t(
      scale(
        t(expr_annotated)
      )
    )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Sample annotation
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    anno_df <- datTraits[
      sample_order,
      ,
      drop = FALSE
    ]

    ann_col <- HeatmapAnnotation(
      cluster = anno_df$cluster,
      col = list(
        cluster = cluster_colors
      )
    )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Create heatmap
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    ht <- Heatmap(
      expr_annotated_z,

      name = "Z-score",

      top_annotation = ann_col,

      cluster_rows = TRUE,

      # Keep samples ordered as
      # Cluster 1 -> Cluster 2 -> Cluster 3
      cluster_columns = FALSE,

      show_column_names = FALSE,

      show_row_names = TRUE,

      row_names_gp = grid::gpar(
        fontsize = 7
      ),

      column_title = paste0(
        "Annotated Hub Genes: ",
        trait_name,
        " ",
        direction_name
      ),

      row_title = paste0(
        nrow(expr_annotated_z),
        " genes"
      )
    )


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Save PNG
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    png_file <- paste0(
      "AnnotatedHubGenes_",
      trait_name,
      "_",
      direction_name,
      "_Heatmap.png"
    )

    png(
      filename = file.path(
        output_dir,
        png_file
      ),
      width = 2200,
      height = 1800,
      res = 200
    )

    draw(ht)

    dev.off()


    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Save PDF
    # -----------------------------------------------------

    pdf_file <- paste0(
      "AnnotatedHubGenes_",
      trait_name,
      "_",
      direction_name,
      "_Heatmap.pdf"
    )

    pdf(
      file = file.path(
        output_dir,
        pdf_file
      ),
      width = 11,
      height = 9
    )

    draw(ht)

    dev.off()


    cat(
      "Saved:",
      csv_file,
      ",",
      png_file,
      ",",
      pdf_file,
      "\n"
    )
  }

} else {

  message(
    "annotated_core was not generated. ",
    "Annotated hub-gene heatmaps were skipped."
  )
}
```
